candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — glaucoma risk and vision screening
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that glaucoma can be asymptomatic early and that comprehensive dilated eye examination is important for detection in people at increased risk.

options.A: Glaucoma may have no early symptoms, and a comprehensive dilated eye examination can detect disease before additional irreversible vision loss occurs.
options.B: Glaucoma reliably produces severe eye pain before optic-nerve damage, so examination is unnecessary in an asymptomatic high-risk person.
options.C: A routine blood test detects glaucoma earlier than an eye examination and is the preferred test for people at increased risk.
options.D: Glaucoma develops only after severe central vision loss is present, so examination before visual symptoms has little value.

candidate.rationale: NEI states that glaucoma often has no early symptoms, symptoms can progress so slowly that a person may not notice them, and the way to find out whether glaucoma is present is a comprehensive dilated eye examination. NEI's screening statement specifically says detection in higher-risk individuals is best done through a comprehensive dilated eye exam. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Glaucoma may be asymptomatic early, and comprehensive dilated eye examination is the recommended detection approach for individuals at increased risk.
candidate.source_document_title: National Eye Institute Statement on Detection of Glaucoma and Adult Vision Screening; Glaucoma
